Parcel & NG911 Data QA: Sheboygan County

Python and PostGIS run side by side on the same county data

Author

James Krauska

Published

November 6, 2026

Summary

The toolkit checks 63,391 tax parcels, 61,811 active address points and 9,852 road centerline segments from Sheboygan County’s public GIS services for 19 kinds of error that matter to land records and NG911 call routing. It found 1,323 items to review.

The same 19 checks are written twice: once in Python (GeoPandas) and once as spatial SQL views in PostgreSQL 18.6 with PostGIS 3.6.2. On this run the two versions agree on every check: 1,323 findings in Python, 1,323 in SQL.

Rates are per 1,000 features of the layer the check looks at (parcels, address points or road segments). Checks with zero findings are kept in the table: a clean result is a result.

Where the findings are

Findings cluster where addresses and small parcels are dense: the City of Sheboygan, Plymouth, Sheboygan Falls and the villages. Rural strings of findings usually follow one road segment whose address range is wrong, which shows up as a run of “number outside road range” findings.

Per address, two rural towns stand out. In the Town of Lyndon, 39 address points sit outside their road segment’s number range and 28 sit unusually far from the segment they are linked to: a handful of segments with wrong ranges or wrong links flag whole strings of rural addresses. The Town of Lima shows the same pattern on a smaller scale.

Check Finding Feature Detail
A03 Outside every parcel SID-19300 Point is not inside any tax parcel
A05 Street name mismatch SID-10429 Point says ‘Indiana Ave’, road segment says ‘S 23rd St’
A06 Number outside road range SID-1040 3034 is outside the segment’s ranges (3100–3198 this side, 3101–3199 other side); it fits nearby segment RD-1888 (28 m away), so the road link may be wrong
A07 Wrong side of the road SID-1006 523 is on the left side, but the left range is 500–598
A08 Far from its road SID-16981 517 m from its road segment
A10 Municipality mismatch SID-23671 Point says ‘Town of Sherman’, boundary says ‘Village of Random Lake’
P01 Overlapping parcels 59002007451 / 59002007554 Parcels 59002007451 and 59002007554 overlap by 613 m²
P02 Gap between parcels Gap of 1 m² between parcels
P04 Missing required attribute 59002011174 Field ‘OWNERNME1’ is empty
P05 Sliver parcel 59010127980 Sliver about 1.2 m wide, 119 m²
P06 Invalid geometry 59012156620 Invalid polygon geometry: Ring Self-intersection[677058.66375846 357602.054499958]
R01 Mixed parity range RD-12574 Left range 4–7 mixes odd and even
R02 Overlapping ranges RD-10122 / RD-5166 Even ranges 5990–6058 and 6050–6078 overlap
R03 Missing range RD-10014 Jolliet Trl segment has no address range, but 3 address(es) link to it

Every finding has a point on the map and a sentence that says what to look at. Three patterns explain most of them:

  • Number outside road range (the largest group) usually means the road segment’s range is too short, or the point is linked to the wrong segment. When a nearby segment of the same street does fit the number, the detail says so.
  • Gaps and overlaps between parcels are a few square meters each: digitizing slivers where neighboring parcels were drawn at different times.
  • Missing attributes are mostly parcels without an owner or municipality that are not road right-of-way.

How the database is built

Schema Table Rows
core address_points 61,811
core municipalities 42
core parcels 63,391
core road_centerlines 9,852
lkp address_status 1
lkp muni_type 3
lkp qa_check 19
lkp road_class 7
lkp road_status 4
lkp settings 4
  • src holds the four layers exactly as downloaded, reprojected to Wisconsin Transverse Mercator (EPSG:3071, meters) so distance and area thresholds match the Python version.
  • lkp holds lookup tables, the database version of geodatabase domains: address status, road class and status (which roads are expected to carry address ranges), municipality types, the check list and the thresholds.
  • core holds typed, constrained copies: primary keys, foreign keys to the lookups, CHECK constraints on address ranges, typed geometry columns, a repaired geometry next to the original, generated columns for normalized street names, and GiST spatial indexes.
  • qa holds one materialized view per check, all with the same four columns (check_code, feature_id, detail, geom), plus qa.findings (every finding as one point layer, used by ArcGIS Pro) and qa.summary.

How to rerun

activate arcgispro-py3-qa
cd ParcelQA_postgis
REM download the layers, load them into PostGIS, run the SQL checks
python postgis\load_postgis.py config\sheboygan.json
REM run the Python checks on the same files
python parcel_qa.py config\sheboygan.json out
REM build this report (HTML and PDF)
set PGPASSWORD=<postgres password>
quarto render report\parcel_qa_report.qmd

When the county updates its data, these steps rebuild every number, table and map in this report.

Rendered November 6, 2026 from PostgreSQL 18.6, PostGIS 3.6.2. Data: Sheboygan County GIS public map services.
